subject: Contingency runbook & keying approach for on-prem deployment - alternatives to escrow
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmehealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Contingency plan and operator access for private deployment

Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal here pushed back on an unconditional escrow clause in the MSA for our on-prem deployment. They asked whether Redwood can provide an alternative approach that preserves our ability to recover service in a provider bankruptcy / cessation scenario without full source-code escrow.

Specifically they asked for:
- A "contingency runbook" describing steps, access windows, and evidence we can expect to obtain if Redwood is unable to operate the private deployment.
- An operator-credentialing matrix showing how operator accounts would be created, scoped, and time-limited.
- Evidence that keys (or key shares) used for startup can be recovered with attestation rather than escrowing full source.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has precedent for: JIT operator access, signed attestation (not escrow) for keying, and a runbook that would be shared under an NDA / addendum?

Jordan
Jordan Miles
Head of Procurement, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency plan and operator access for private deployment

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we have an "escrow-light" pathway we use for regulated customers that avoids source escrow but provides operational continuity. High level:

- Contingency runbook: a signed, versioned runbook we can share under NDA that lists recovery steps, roles, artifact checklist (snapshots, signed manifests), and communications cadence.
- Operator access: we provision time-limited operator roles via our JIT workflow (MFA + approve/record) with auditable session logs. We can include an operator-access matrix that maps actions to minimal role scopes.
- Keying & attestation: we can offer an HSM-backed split-key model where Redwood holds an encrypted HSM share and the customer holds a second share, plus a notarized attestation workflow for key handover in contingency events.

I'll loop in Laura (Legal) and Dev (Technical ops) to propose deliverables and a short timeline. We can prepare a draft runbook and a proposed MSA addendum with redline options for the operator annex.

Next steps: Laura — can your team draft the addendum language outline? Dev — can you confirm what artifacts we can commit to deliver under a contingency (snapshots, signed manifests, runbook, audit logs)?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmehealth.com>
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency plan and operator access for private deployment

Jordan / team —

Thanks, Tessa. Jordan, we can do an alternative to traditional source-code escrow that addresses Acme's risk profile. Proposed approach (outline):

1) Operator Access Annex (MSA Addendum):
   - Define "Operator Account" lifecycle: request -> JIT approval -> session recording -> automatic expiry.
   - Limitations: no shell-level access to customer data; access constrained to specified recovery procedures.

2) Contingency Runbook (deliverable):
   - High-level recovery steps, required artifacts (latest encrypted model snapshot, signed KV manifest, bootstrap configs).
   - Timelines for Redwood to respond and for handover actions (e.g., 48-hour evidence package delivery).

3) Keying & Attestation:
   - HSM split-key proposal (Redwood + Customer shares).
   - If customers prefer not to hold a share, Redwood can store shares with a neutral third-party depositary and provide a notarized attestation + cryptographic proof-of-possession on request.

4) Evidence and Audit:
   - We can commit to encrypted snapshots plus signed manifests and session logs; SOC2 reports and select audit artifacts will be shared under NDA.

I'll attach a proposed addendum skeleton and suggested redlines focusing on scope and remediation triggers. Markus, flag anything tax/finance relevant? Dev, please confirm the list of artifacts you can guarantee and the expected production-to-evidence time window.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmehealth.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency plan and operator access for private deployment

Jordan / Laura / Tessa —

Confirming technical commitments we can include in the runbook addendum:

- Artifacts: encrypted model snapshot (AES-GCM), signed KV manifest (SHA256 + Redwood key), runtime config bundle, operator session logs (W3C formatted) and job replay instructions.
- Delivery SLA in contingency: preliminary package within 48 hours of a validated trigger; full handover (including transfer instructions and decryption assist) within 10 business days.
- Operator access: JIT provisioning using Okta workflows + hardware MFA; each session recorded and checksumed with an append-only log.
- Keying options: HSM split-key (recommended) OR split-of-secrets with customer-held share. We can also provide a notarized attestation packet signed by Redwood legal and the custodian of the third-party depositary.

Attachments: operator-access-matrix.xlsx (example roles / allowed actions), contingency-runbook-v1.pdf (skeleton).

If the customer wants the notarized-depositary route, we'll need a short statement in the addendum identifying acceptable depositaries. Otherwise the HSM split-key path is simplest operationally.

- Dev

From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 17 Mar 2027 14:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contingency plan and operator access for private deployment

Thanks — this is helpful and much closer to what our legal team was hoping to see. A few quick items from our side:

- The 48-hour preliminary SLA is acceptable, subject to an objective "validated trigger" definition. We'll propose wording that includes material cessation of Redwood operations, insolvency filings, or failure to respond to a formal escalation for >7 days.
- For keying we prefer the HSM split-key approach. Can you add language that the HSM will be FIPS 140-2 level 3 or equivalent and that any third-party custodians meet SOC2 Type II?
- We'll review the attachments and send a short redline to the proposed addendum.

If you can give us a draft addendum (redlineable) and the runbook skeleton under NDA by next Tuesday (23 March), we'll aim to return marked feedback by end of that week.

Jordan
